result.title: Kolpona: An Agentic Framework with Gradient-Free Neuron Programming for RTL Generation
result.summary: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) for register-transfer level (RTL) design are usually improved by fine-tuning on curated Verilog corpora, which needs large sets of verified designs and GPU training. We present Kolpona, an agentic framework that improves such models without gradient training. Its first component is neuron programming, a new form of weight-space programming (WSP) that writes single neurons in closed form into the weights to remove failure habits found on practice tasks, and keeps each edit only when testbench results on fresh tasks favour it. At inference time, tool-using agents propose designs, and a label-free selection stage delivers one design per task from the specification, the candidates and their simulations alone. On Qwen3.5-4B, edits to 16 neurons raise the VerilogEval v2 pass@1 of the model alone from 31.7% to 55.4%, and the full framework reaches 77.6%. On Qwen3.8-27B, Kolpona lifts pass@1 from 73.1% to 94.9% on VerilogEval v2 and from 66.0% to 92.0% on RTLLM v2.1 on a single 32 GB GPU, above every published system in our comparison. The RTL edits also carry over to Python and raise the pass@1 of the 4B model alone from 84.8% to 91.5% on HumanEval+ and from 67.7% to 77.5% on MBPP+.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Kolpona 框架，用无梯度的「神经元编程」以闭式方式直接改写模型中的单个神经元权重来消除失败习惯，并以新任务上的测试平台结果决定是否保留编辑；推理时由工具型 agent 产生多个设计，再由无标签选择阶段仅凭规格与仿真结果挑出一个。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属 RTL 代码生成、非视觉推理，但「闭式编辑个别神经元并只在验证通过时保留」可供核查为定点修正内部失败状态的训练/编辑线索，「多候选＋仿真无标签选择」则与 latent 推理轨迹的搜索验证和贡献分配问题相通。
